newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stock index sets record in mixed market.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stock index sets record in mixed market.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange's key index set another record close on Tuesday, extending Monday's gains despite a sluggish session.
The TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 8.86 points to 6801.17, its 29th record finish of the year.
But the overall market was mixed. Declining stocks outnumbered advances 511 to 484, with 293 issues unchanged.
Strength in energy, real estate, retailing and forestry products was partly offset by profit-taking in conglomerates and precious metals.
Just more than 90 million shares were traded for a total value of C$1.57 billion ($1.1 billion).
Analysts said the market had the momentum for further gains, but high stock valuations had many investors pondering when a correction would occur.
"If we're going to have a major pullback, I would guess later this year. Possibly in the fourth quarter or the first quarter of 1998," said Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram.
* Prudential Steel Ltd. jumped 5.25 to 52.50 on better than expected second-quarter earnings and a 3-for-1 stock split.
* Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce added 0.25 to 38.85 after the bank agreed to tender its 10 percent stake in National Trustco to Bank of Nova Scotia's acquisition bid.
* Gold stocks were depressed by weaker prices. COMEX August gold fell $3.60 to $329.80 an ounce. Euro-Nevada Mining Corp. Ltd. sank 1 to 42.50.
Placer Dome Inc. slipped 0.30 to 23.10. Placer earlier revised the sale terms for its Val d'Or assets in Canada to reflect the current weakness in gold markets.
* Algoma Steel Inc. lost 0.80 to 8.75 after reporting slightly weaker second-quarter earnings.
